failures.criterion: CI is green at the head under test: the envoy-session-stall lane, which the ci-ok condenser reads, is red at f41a4d8c
failures.evidence: Run 41167627270, job 124443217959, step 'Stall test of claude-envoy': `error: the listener exited (1): … 2026/10/31 05:12:38 listen tcp 127.0.0.1:43779: bind: address already in use`, at packages/envoy-client/test/envoy-stack.ts:100 (awaitReady) from startEnvoyStack. THE CAUSE, measured, not guessed: `freePort()` (envoy-stack.ts:67) opens a probe socket on port 0, reads the port and CLOSES the probe before the next call opens its own, and `startEnvoyStack` calls it three times in a row for natsd's client port, natsd's monitoring port and the listener's (envoy-stack.ts:183-187). The kernel may hand the same ephemeral port to two of those probes, after which natsd binds it and the listener's bind fails with exactly that error. I ran the harness's own freePort body 2,000 times in triples in this pod: 1 triple repeated a port (`duplicate triple: [ 64019, 56466, 56466 ]`). The helper and its three calls are byte-identical to main's, so the race pre-dates this branch, but the file is one this tree changes (104 lines, the listener-grant option), the lane is red at the head I tested, and the fix belongs in this pull request. THE RED TEST: packages/envoy-client/src/__tests__/free-ports.test.ts, commit d8eecf87e14b, pushed. It fails now for want of the fix — `bun test packages/envoy-client/src/__tests__/free-ports.test.ts` gives `SyntaxError: Export named 'freePorts' not found in module …/test/envoy-stack.ts`, 1 fail — and asks for one seam: a `freePorts(count)` that chooses every port with all its probe sockets open and only then closes them. Its two cases are that the three ports differ over 2,000 rounds and that each is free when it is handed back, the second so that a fix which keeps the probes open cannot pass.

verifiedAtThisHead.what: A hold delays only the session that holds, and the held message is pushed once the other push ends unlanded
verifiedAtThisHead.command: A scratch test of mine in cmd/listener (not committed): two serving-port sessions on consumer delivery, each following a topic of its own; an attempt record recorded for the first session's message with no push behind it; then the second session's message published while the first is held.
verifiedAtThisHead.observed: PASS, 3.84s. The listener logs 'session relay holds a message another path is pushing' for the held session; the other session's port takes its own message while that hold stands; the held session's port has been pushed nothing at that moment; and when the attempt record is cleared, the held message reaches the port once and is not pushed again within 2 s. The structural reason is that each relay runs on a goroutine of its own under a sync.WaitGroup with no limit (session_relay.go:181, start at :535).
verifiedAtThisHead.negativeControl: Two, each of which made the scratch test fail. (1) Isolation really measured: I serialized the judgement across sessions by taking one package-level mutex around holdWhilePushedElsewhere in pushUntilAccepted — FAIL, 'the other session's message … never reached its port while ses_held_… held one'. (2) The hold really holds: with the attempt record never cleared — FAIL, 'the held message … never reached the port after the other push ended'. Both reverted. The scratch test was deleted rather than committed: it found no defect, and a test commit restarts the whole CI run, which the architect's 00:31Z rule says to spend only when it is needed. It is three dozen lines and the implementer is welcome to land it as a regression lock in the next code round at no extra CI cost.
